This delivers the code-side half of the strategy's keyboard conformance goal and produces the fixed state that the updated conformance documentation will describe. ## Scope - Fix each keyboard-accessibility defect enumerated in the audit report for the four audited flows in the Dashboard (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission): - Restore/manage focus correctly in modals (focus moved into the modal on open, trapped while open, returned to the invoking control on close). - Make every control reachable and operable via keyboard (tab order, keyboard activation for custom controls). - Apply the consistent focus-indicator treatment across all interactive controls in the audited flows so focus visibility is uniform. - Verify each audited flow end-to-end using keyboard-only interaction. - Out of scope: screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require, and any flow outside the four audited ones. ## Acceptance Criteria - Given the project creation flow, when the user completes it using keyboard input only, then every step is operable, no control is unreachable, and no focus trap occurs. - Given the workbench spawn flow, when the user completes it using keyboard input only, then every step is operable, no control is unreachable, and no focus trap occurs. - Given the model deployment flow, when the user completes it using keyboard input only, then every step is operable, no control is unreachable, and no focus trap occurs. - Given the pipeline run submission flow, when the user completes it using keyboard input only, then every step is operable, no control is unreachable, and no focus trap occurs. - Given any interactive control within the four audited flows, when it receives keyboard focus, then a visible focus indicator is rendered using a consistent treatment across all such controls. - Every keyboard-related defect item in the audit report for the four audited flows is resolved or explicitly dispositioned (fixed / not applicable with reason). ## HLR Traceability - **HLR-1 (P1)**: The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls. - **HLR-2 (P1)**: Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows. The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented fixes before republishing. ## Scope - Update the VPAT conformance statement to reflect the keyboard operability and focus-indicator state of the four audited Dashboard flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) after remediation. - Update the product documentation accessibility statement to describe the current accessibility posture of the audited flows. - Republish both documents through the Red Hat docs content process so the public conformance statement is current. - Obtain technical review of the updated content against the implemented fixes. - Out of scope: conformance claims for flows or criteria outside the four audited keyboard-operability fixes. ## Acceptance Criteria - The VPAT is updated to accurately reflect the fixed keyboard-operability state of the four audited flows and is republished. - The product docs accessibility statement is updated and republished to reflect the same fixed state. - The updated documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented keyboard-accessibility fixes, and the review outcome is recorded (reviewer sign-off or documented review comments resolved). - The published conformance documentation contains no claims that contradict the implemented state of the four audited flows. ## HLR Traceability - **HLR-3 (P2)**: The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review. This edge does not trigger priority inheritance per the docs-authoring priority exception. | ## HLR Traceability Matrix | HLR | Priority | Epic(s) | Coverage | |-----|----------|---------|----------| | HLR-1 | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Four audited flows fully keyboard-operable, no focus traps or unreachable controls | | HLR-2 | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Consistent visible focus indicators across the audited flows | | HLR-3 | P2 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | VPAT and accessibility statement updated and republished with technical review | All HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements. ## Epic Boundary Decisions - **HLR-1 and HLR-2 consolidated into one epic**: both requirements apply to the same four Dashboard flows, the same UI surfaces (modals, forms, controls), the same team, and the same change (remediating the audit's per-flow defect list). Focus-trap and unreachable-control fixes and focus-indicator consistency are remediated on the same surfaces in the same review cycle; splitting them would force two epics to touch the same components independently. Both are P1, so no priority split is involved. - **HLR-3 as a separate `docs-authoring` epic**: updating and republishing the VPAT and the product docs accessibility statement is substantive content authoring (a conformance document and a rewritten docs topic), a distinct work-product type from code implementation, and affects a different component (Documentation). Per the docs-authoring priority exception, its priority derives from the strategy frontmatter `priority: Normal` → P2. ## Investigation Epics None. The strategy states there are no open questions — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow, so no unknown changes which epics exist or what they do. ## Health Warnings - **Missing strategy sections** (non-blocking): the strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no Dependencies table, no formal Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, and no Non-Functional Requirements section. Epic acceptance criteria were derived from the HLRs and the problem statement instead. - **Team ownership inferred**: the strategy does not state owning teams. E001's team (RHOAI Dashboard) is taken from the Dashboard architecture context file; E002's team (RHOAI Documentation) is inferred for the docs content process. Verify with stakeholders. - **Docs priority vs. business urgency**: HLR-3 is P2 by the docs-authoring priority exception (strategy priority Normal), but the problem statement ties the published VPAT to two public-sector customer renewals — the business deadline may be tighter than P2 suggests. Flagged for human verification, not re-prioritized. - **Scope trap (minor)**: screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require and flows outside the four audited ones are explicitly out of scope; the implementation epic must resist scope creep from the full audit report if it contains defects beyond keyboard operability.
